text:
Twilight water, thirsty water,

the late birds leave you like syllables.

Swaying in the poplars, the wind subtracts from you

the happiness of your eyes drinking themselves in mine.


I allied my thought to your shadowy joys

and tasted the sweetness of your slow words.

You lengthened twilights in my thirsty hands:

I devoured your tragic summers in the bread.


My hands will remain moist from your breast.

From my stubbornness the poison will remain to you,

floating flower of anguish that destiny baptized.


From our two silences one day must spring

the luminous water that gives a divine blue

to the depth of cypresses of your soul and mine.

translation.title: On Leaving a Soul
translation.editorial_note: This alternate-title variant keeps the same twilight-water sonnet and its luminous future water.
